newsitem.title: USA: US Trade Rep calls U.S.-China trade gap disturbing.
newsitem.headline: US Trade Rep calls U.S.-China trade gap disturbing.

text.p: Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky Friday called the U.S. trade deficit with China "disturbing" and said the United States must continue to act aggressively to open access to Chinese markets.

"We have some significant work to do with China. The deficit number is disturbing," Barshefsky told a House appropriations subcommittee. "We believe we have to continue to be aggressive (with) China on market access."
U.S. data showed the U.S. trade deficit with China swelling to nearly $40 billion last year, up 17 percent from a year earlier. The issue ranks as a top trade concern in Congress.
Barshefsky said China has yet to remove enough trade barriers to earn admission to the World Trade Organization.
"Has China earned WTO entry at this point? No," she told lawmakers.

She stressed that China would have to agree to substantially open markets at the time of entry into the WTO and would not be able to gain entry by promising to open markets at some point in the future.
"We will have to see very substantial market opening on entry into the WTO," she said.
Barshefsky said she was hopeful that the Clinton administration would be ready "shortly" to offer Congress a proposal on fast-track trade negotiating authority.
"I think we're going to be moving very expeditiously on this," she said in response to a lawmaker's question.
The authority, which is granted by Congress, would allow the administration to negotiate trade agreements without fear they will be changed later by Congress.
The recently confirmed trade chief said she plans to restructure the agency, making some personnel changes "to keep people fresh" but not doing "anything particularly radical."
She reiterated that agriculture will be a top priority for the agency and said she plans to bring in a higher level agricultural trade negotiator than the agency has had in the past.
